course_title: Practice & Research in Physiotherapy Across the Lifespan 1
course_description: The course will provide students with core knowledge of healthy and disease-related ageing processes across musculoskeletal, neurological, and sensory systems in older populations. The course uses a combination of lectures, video presentations, case studies, practical classes, and independent learning packages. Students will gain professional competencies in: conducting client interviews; assessing and identifying changes in movement and posture which are within or outside the expectations of normal ageing parameters; prescribing appropriate management strategies including exercise and; understanding current clinical guidelines, policy and practice related to the older person. Specialty areas addressed in the course include falls prevention, dizziness (vestibular rehabilitation), women’s and men's health, oncology, palliative care, pharmacology, and psychiatry.

course_aims: This course aims to enable you to:

learning_outcomes.description: Apply knowledge of healthy and disease-related ageing processes affecting the musculoskeletal, neurological, and sensory systems to select appropriate client assessments, and develop and implement client-centred treatment programs.
Communicate effectively with older clients, including those with cognitive impairment, as well as families, carers, and other health professionals to support assessment and management.
Apply the ICF framework to guide and underpin the planning of assessment and the development of client-centred rehabilitation goals in older people.
Apply clinical reasoning and technical skills to plan and deliver physiotherapy management for older adults with multi-pathologies and disability.

Apply clinical reasoning and advanced knowledge of falls risk factors to develop management and prevention programs for complex older clients in diverse settings, aligned with current evidence, professional guidelines, and relevant policies.
Apply clinical reasoning and technical skills to plan and deliver physiotherapy management for clients with a life-limiting illness, and use self-management strategies to respond to grief and loss.
Identify common psychiatric conditions and behaviours and explain their impact on physiotherapy management strategies.
Describe common health concerns experienced by men and explain the role of physiotherapy management in Men's Health.
Apply clinical reasoning and technical skills to safely and effectively assess and manage women during pregnancy, postnatal recovery, and for continence, pelvic pain, and menopause.

assessment_details.title: Reflective Journal Communication with Older People
assessment_details.task_description: Students are required to complete a journal entry, reflecting on their experience conducting a medical interview of a self-sourced older person, specifically focusing on their communication skills. In no more than 700 words , students are expected to describe their experience interviewing an older person. The following points should be used to guide the reflective piece: How did the interview go overall? Did you encounter any challenges? Did you obtain all the clinical/personal information required? What questions, if any, remained unanswered and why? What did you think of your ability to show empathy and demonstrate active listening? What would you do differently to establish rapport when talking to an older person/client for the first time, who is not familiar to you? Did you conclude the interview with a clear understanding of the older person’s (health-related) goals and priorities? What would you benefit from working on over the next 12 months to improve your interview skills, how will you do this and how will you know you have improved? Students are also required to attach a copy of their interview notes – i.e. completed UQ Neurological, Ageing and Balance (NAB) Clinic Assessment Form – to support their journal entry. The interview notes MUST remain anonymous. Under no circumstances should identifiable clinical information be uploaded to open or external AI platforms, as it is unethical and irresponsible. Given this assessment is related to a placement with clinical information please see more information on use of AI in student placements under additional assessment information. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 13 (27 Jul - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Practical Classes Weekly, 2-hour in-person practical classes on campus will enable students to apply knowledge and skills to clinical scenarios, encompassing the assessment and delivery of treatment techniques in older populations, adults with life-limiting illness, and women during pregnancy. To prepare, please consult the Blackboard site to complete any associated online preparation tasks before each practical class, such as reviewing videos and practical class instructions.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 6 (27 Jul - 06 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Physiotherapy for ageing and complex care This weekly, 3-hour lecture series of pre-recorded online educational material is designed to enable flexible, independent learning, which is to be viewed prior to that week's practical class. The content will focus on preparing the student to work as an effective, empathetic and evidence-based physiotherapist to manage older clients. It will provide students with foundational knowledge of ageing body systems in health and disease and how these contribute to functional decline such as vestibular dysfunction, frailty, falls, confusion and dementia. A more detailed understanding of vestibular dysfunction and balance impairment will be gained, including conducting an efficient, effective, client-centred physiotherapy assessment and implementing safe and effective evidence-based interventions. Finally, the role of the physiotherapist and practical considerations for providing optimal physiotherapy services for older clients in the community and residential aged care will be explored.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 7 To Week 9 (07 Sep - 27 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Oncology & Palliative Care This weekly, 3-hour lecture series of pre-recorded online educational material is designed to enable flexible, independent learning, which is to be viewed prior to that week's practical class. This lecture series will provide students with knowledge of oncology and palliative care, including physiotherapy assessment techniques and multidisciplinary management approaches (including psychiatry) and; advanced communication skills for interacting with clients with life-limiting illness.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 10 To Week 13 (05 Oct - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Women's & Men's Health This weekly, 3-hour lecture series of pre-recorded online educational material is designed to enable flexible, independent learning, which is to be viewed prior to that week's practical class. This lecture series will provide students with knowledge of physiotherapy assessment and management techniques for the antenatal and postnatal stages of pregnancy, continence, pelvic pain, and menopause. Students will also develop knowledge of health concerns specific to men.
